MINUTES
  Regular Meeting
  ALHAMBRA CITY COUNCIL
  Council Chambers, 111 South First Street
  September 9, 2024

ROLL CALL: At 6:08 p.m., on Monday, September 9, 2024, the Alhambra City Council met in Council
Chambers of the Alhambra City Hall.

PRESENT:  LEE, MALONEY, ANDRADE-STADLER, MAZA
ABSENT:  PÉREZ

Officials Present: City Manager Binnquist, Deputy City Manager Hembree, City Attorney Montes,
City Clerk Myles, Director of Parks and Recreation Macias, Director of Library Services LohGuan,
Chief of Police Kennedy, Chief of Fire Department Ragusa, Director of Finance Lieu, Director of
Human Resources Ko, Director of Community Development Ho, Director of Public Works and Utilities
Ahlen, Management Analyst Martel, Code Enforcement Supervisor Perez-Garcia

FLAG SALUTE:  Led by Vice Mayor Lee

LAND ACKNOWLEDGEMENT

PRESENTATIONS

1.  ALHAMBRA FRIENDSHIP CITY POLICY DRAFT – F2M24-7

  Deputy City Manager HEMBREE delivered a staff report. On July 22, 2024, staff presented
  information about Alhambra’s Sister Cities which include: Granada, Spain; Hsin-Chuang,
  Taiwan, Republic of China; Sanya City, People’s Republic of China; and Kirishima, Japan.
  Additionally, information about Sister Cities International and an overview of neighboring Cities
  programs and/or policies were presented. Following the presentation, Council directed staff to
  look into the City of San Gabriel and City of Arcadia’s Sister City and/or Friendship Policy or
  Programs and provide a draft Policy for consideration of a Friendship City Program Policy for
  Alhambra. Staff reviewed Sister and Friendship City Policies to provide context and reported
  findings to the City Council as well as presented a draft Alhambra Friendship City Policy for
  Council’s consideration and comments.

  Discussion: Councilmember MALONEY supported the draft in terms of flexibility for
  procedures, suggested more leniency on the side of the Sister City response, suggested a
  formal statement of affirmation from the Sister Cities, and agreed with the ambassador
  requirement but cautioned against termination for not continuing the position.

  Councilmember ANDRADE-STADLER supported the draft and agreed with Mr. Maloney’s
  suggestions. She also suggested the sharing of flags between cities.

  Councilmember MAZA supported the draft and further suggested continued flexibility and
  adaptability through the years.

  Vice Mayor LEE discussed the structure of the procedure and the purpose of the program to
  reflect the diversity of Alhambra resident’s backgrounds. She suggested adding language
  regarding establishing relationships with governments around the globe except those who
  have no relations with the United States which would enforce reasonable limits to the extent
  of the program. She also suggested clarifying that Councilmembers and community members
  1
9-9-24
   from the San Gabriel Valley could sponsor an organization which did not have to be a
  registered non-profit. She agreed with Mr. Maloney’s suggestion to reduce the initial start-up
  paperwork. Ms. HEMBREE clarified that rather than an agreement or resolution from the
  responding Sister City, that they could instead document the relationship by a statement of
  affirmation or include an agreement or resolution. Ms. LEE stressed the need to streamline
  the process and to adapt the policy as needed. With regards to sharing information with a
  Sister City, Ms. LEE expressed caution and suggested that any written letters or shared
  information be approved by the City Council during a public hearing to protect city interests.
  She supported Ms. Andrade-Stadler’s suggestion of sharing national flags and requested that
  language be included that the flags would be displayed in Alhambra.

  Ms. ANDRADE-STADLER discussed the flexibility of the program to add additional cities and
  the inclusion of cities within Latin American countries and the country of Vietnam. Mr.
  MALONEY referred to Ms. Lee’s comments regarding eligible countries and stated that
  international relationships change over time and that future City Councils should have flexibility
  to make connections through other international cities. He related his experiences visiting
  Kirishima and the informal non-obligatory system which avoided undue constraints on other
  cities. Ms. LEE and City Attorney MONTES discussed the possibility of Councilmembers
  extending relationships with countries not associated with the United States. Mr. MONTES
  stated that any relationship would have to be discussed and approved by Council as a whole.
  Ms. LEE allowed that the decision to extend relationships to other countries would be left up
  to Council approval.

  Ms. ANDRADE-STADLER motioned to approve the Alhambra Friendship City Policy with
  included changes suggested by Council including: language concerning San Gabriel Valley
  community sponsoring organization, that the friendship city relationships be documented by a
  statement of affirmation from an authorised official which may include an agreement or
  resolution, sharing opportunities to promote prosperity and quality of life including letters, and
  eliminate 6B.

  Action Taken:  City Council reviewed the draft Alhambra Friendship City Policy and
  provided direction to staff, and approved the Alhambra Friendship City Policy with included
  changes suggested by Council including: language concerning San Gabriel Valley community
  sponsoring organization, that the friendship city relationships be documented by a statement
  of affirmation from an authorised official which may include an agreement or resolution, sharing
  opportunities to promote prosperity and quality of life including letters, and eliminate 6B of the
  draft Policy.

  Vote:  Moved:  ANDRADE-STADLER  Seconded:  MAZA
  Ayes:  MAZA, MALONEY, ANDRADE-STADLER, LEE,
  Noes:  NONE
  Absent:  PÉREZ

CONSENT AGENDA (Item Nos. 2 – 11)

All items listed under the Consent Agenda were considered by the City Council to be routine were
enacted by one motion.

2.  ACCEPT QUITCLAIM DEED FROM ALHAMBRA UNIFIED SCHOOL DISTRICT TO
DEDICATE A PORTION OF SHORB STREET TO CITY OF ALHAMBRA – F2M24-8,
F2M22-65, D2M24-2034, M2M24-164

  As part of the Shorb Community Center project, the portion of Shorb Street between 6th Street
  and 7th Street would be vacated and incorporated into the community center project.
  2
9-9-24
   Eastbound Shorb Street would terminate around 7th Street while northbound and southbound
  6th Street would have no access to Shorb Street. The underlying fee to the street belonged to
  the Alhambra Unified School District. The City had conversations with the School District
  about the project and requested that the portion of Shorb Street be dedicated to the City to
  facilitate the project. On July 23, 2024 the Alhambra Unified School District Board of Education
  approved the dedication of a portion of Shorb Street to the City of Alhambra through a quitclaim
  deed. Accepting the quitclaim deed would be the first step in the street vacation process which
  would be processed at a future date along with the Community Center project.

  Discussion:  None.

  Action Taken:  City Council accepted the quitclaim deed from the Alhambra Unified
  School District and authorize the City Clerk to sign the Certificate of Acceptance, directed the
  City Clerk to record the appropriate documents and directed staff to undertake the steps
  necessary to finalize the Council’s actions. (M2M24-164)

  Vote:  Moved:  ANDRADE-STADLER  Seconded:  MAZA
  Ayes:  MAZA, MALONEY, ANDRADE-STADLER, LEE
  Noes:  NONE
  Absent:  PÉREZ

3.  APPROVAL OF HELICOPTER LAW ENFORCEMENT SEVICES AGREEMENT –
  F2M22-46, C2M22-18, C2M24-55, M2M24-165

  On May 9, 2022, the City Council approved an agreement with the County of Los Angeles to
  utilize air support services for non-life threatening or non-mutual aid incidents through June
  20, 2027. The Los Angeles County Sheriff’s Department recently worked internally to
  streamline their processes and requested a new agreement be approved by the City to cover
  the same services with a new 5-year term and updated FY 2024-25 rates. In response, staff
  requested to close the current agreement (C2M22-18) and the Council approve a new
  agreement with Los Angeles County. The new agreement would be effective for a 5-year
  period through June 30, 2029, the scope of services would remain the same and the rates
  have been updated. The City would continue to be charged on a per-minute basis based upon
  hourly rate set by the County Auditor-Controller each fiscal year. Annual costs were expected
  to be below $25,500.

  Discussion:  None.

  Action Taken:  City Council approved a Helicopter Law Enforcement Services
  Agreement between the City of Alhambra and the County of Los Angeles for as-needed, non-
  emergent, non-life threatening, and non-mutual aid helicopter law enforcement services for a
  5-year period, through June 30, 2029; authorized the Chief of Police to sign the contract; and,
  directed staff to undertake the steps necessary to finalize Council’s action. (M2M24-165)

  Vote:  Moved:  ANDRADE-STADLER  Seconded:  MAZA
  Ayes:  MAZA, MALONEY, ANDRADE-STADLER, LEE
  Noes:  NONE
  Absent:  PÉREZ

4.  CANCEL AWARD OF CONTRACT: PURCHASE OF ONE 7-YARD DUMP TRUCK FOR THE
  PUBLIC WORKS DEPARTMENT – F2M21-6A, C2M23-3, M2M24-166

  3
9-9-24
   On January 9, 2023, the City Council awarded a contract to purchase a new dump truck for
  the Public Works Department; however, due to the California Air Resources Board’s (CARB)
  latest regulatory emission reduction mandates, Ford Motor Company could not provide the
  truck with a diesel engine option. Beginning on January 1, 2024, all state and local government
  fleets must have ensured that 50% of their vehicle purchases were zero-emissions vehicles.
  By 2027, all vehicle purchases must have been 100% electric. City staff worked on a new
  specification for Notice Inviting Bids on an Electric Dump Truck for the Public Works Division.

  Discussion:  None.

  Action Taken: City Council rescinded the contract with Rush Truck Centers (Contract No.
  C2M23-3) in the amount of $126,948.69; and, directed staff to undertake the steps necessary
  to finalize Council’s action. (M2M24-166)

  Vote:  Moved:  ANDRADE-STADLER  Seconded:  MAZA
  Ayes:  MAZA, MALONEY, ANDRADE-STADLER, LEE

5.  AWARD CONTRACT: PURCHASE OF FIVE POLICE PATROL VEHICLES – F2M24-
6A, C2M24-56, M2M24-167

  The FY 2024-25 budget included the replacement of police patrol vehicles. As such, staff
  sought to purchase five police patrol vehicles through a cooperative purchase agreement to
  replace the aging police vehicles. Cooperative purchase was allowable per Alhambra
  Municipal Code 3.36.080(B)(3). On July 28, 2024, Sourcewell opened four bids for the
  procurement of vehicles, cars, vans, SUVs, and light trucks with related equipment,
  accessories, and services. Sourcewell awarded contract 091521-NAF to National Auto Fleet
  Group on July 28, 2021 – a contract that would not expire until November 8, 2025. Per the
  Sourcewell bid specifications, police vehicles could be purchased. Staff recommended
  purchasing five police vehicles utilizing this option.

  Discussion:  None

  Action Taken:  City Council awarded a contract, subject to final language approval by
  the City Manager and City Attorney, to National Auto Fleet Group for the purchase of five police
  patrol vehicles in the amount of $290,481.50; and, directed staff to undertake the steps
  necessary to finalize Council’s action. (M2M24-167)

  Vote:  Moved:  ANDRADE-STADLER  Seconded:  MAZA
  Ayes:  MAZA, MALONEY, ANDRADE-STADLER, LEE
  Noes:  NONE

9.  SECOND READING AND ADOPTION OF AN ORDINANCE UPDATING THE PRIMA
  FACIE SPEED LIMITS IN THE CITY – F96-33, F2M14-9, O2M24-4839

  The City of Alhambra’s Public Works Department completed an Engineering and Traffic
  Survey (Speed Survey) for 88 street segments citywide and prepared the City of Alhambra
  2023/2024 Engineering and Traffic Survey. The purpose of an engineering and traffic survey
  was to establish updated speed limits that could be legally enforced using radar at pre-
  determined locations. The City of Alhambra’s 2023/2024 Engineering and Traffic Survey
  determined that 9 segment locations are eligible for a 5 MPH reduction in the posted speed
  limit. These segment locations were outlined in the Director of Public Works & Utilities’ August
  26, 2024 staff report. Adoption of an ordinance was necessary to set the speed limits on those
  road segments identified in the report that were outside of a residential district and are not
  otherwise subject to the Vehicle Code’s prima facia speed limit.

10.  SECOND READING OF AN ORDINANCE TO AMEND ALHAMBRA MUNICIPAL CODE
  (AMC) CHAPTER 2.48 OF TITLE II TO IMPLEMENT CHANGES TO PROBATIONARY
PERIOD FOR EMPLOYEES – F2M24-2, O2M24-4838

  Staff requested that the City Council introduce Ordinance No. O2M24-4838 for its second
  reading and adopt the ordinance. This ordinance contained a minor change to the AMC to
  provide City staff (with the approval of the City Council) the flexibility and ability to negotiate a
  different probationary period for employees when appropriate. The ordinance amended
  Section 2.48.120 (Probationary Period) which stated “All original, reinstatement and
  promotional appointments shall be subject to a probationary period of one year,” to and/include
  “unless otherwise negotiated and memorialized in a Memorandum of Understanding with a
  recognized employee bargaining group.”

  Discussion:  None.

  Action Taken:  City Council declared introduced for its second reading and adopt the
  following ordinance entitled:

  Ordinance No. O2M24-4838: An Ordinance of the City Council of the City of
  Alhambra, California amending Chapter 2.48 of Title II of the Alhambra
  Municipal Code to implement changes to probationary period for employees

  Ayes:  MAZA, MALONEY, ANDRADE-STADLER, LEE

 11.  SECOND READING AND ADOPTION OF AN ORDINANCE TO IMPLEMENT
  CALIFORNIA UNIFORM CONSTRUCTION COST ACCOUNTING PROCEDURES FOR
PUBLIC CONSTRUCTION PROJECTS, AMENDMENT TO THE ALHAMBRA  MUNICIPAL
CODE REGARDING PUBLIC CONTRACT CODES AND UPDATING NON- PUBLIC
PROJECTS/PROFESSIONAL SERVICES CONTRACT LIMITS – F2M24-62,  O2M24-4837

  The Public Contract Code specified the procedures that public agencies must follow when
  they build public works projects, including limits on project costs. The California Uniform Public
  Construction Cost Accounting Act (CUPCCAA) was enacted in 1983 as an alternative to these
  general requirements by allowing increased bid limits as long as participating agencies follow
  uniform accounting standards and bidding procedures. Staff requested the City Council “opt
  in” to the provisions set forth by CUPCCAA. This will allow public projects costing $60,000 or
  less to be performed by negotiated contract or by purchase order. Projects costing $200,000
  or less can use informal bidding procedures set forth in CUPCCAA. Projects that cost more
  than $200,000 must be put out to bid under formal bidding procedures. The benefits of
  adopting CUPCCAA will increase the purchasing limit for public agencies, simplify bidding for
  projects that are $200,000 or less, reduce number of formal bids based on project size, and
  expedite contracting for projects under $200,000.In order for the City to avail itself of the higher
  bid and purchasing limits, the City must formally elect to be bound by the provisions of the
  Uniform Public Construction Cost Accounting Act, which specifies the procedures for obtaining
  informal bids, and to use the uniform construction cost accounting procedures adopted by the
  California Uniform Construction Accounting Commission. Staff is requesting the City Council
  adopt Ordinance No. O2M24-4837 and update the City of Alhambra's Purchasing Policy Limits
  as more specifically outlined in the Director of Finance’s August 26, 2024 staff report. Staff is
  requesting that the City Council introduce O2M24-4837 for its second reading and adopt the
  ordinance.

  Discussion:  Vice Mayor LEE and Director of Finance LIEU discussed the ordinance
  and Ms. LIEU responded to Ms. LEE’s concerns regarding the formal and informal purchasing
  process. With regards to Ms. Lee’s concerns with certain language used, City Attorney
  MONTES clarified that the language used in the ordinance was copied directly from State law
  to ensure the City of Alhambra’s compliance with state law. Councilmember MALONEY and
  Councilmember ANDRADE-STADLER suggested that staff provide a quarterly report of
  executed contracts under $60,000. Ms. LEE stressed the need for properly posting all notice
  inviting bids and requests for proposals on the City website and ensure fair access to all
  contract opportunities within the City.

  Action Taken:  City Council declared introduced for its second reading and adopt the
  following ordinance entitled:

  Ordinance No. O2M24-4837: AN ORDINANCE OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF
  THE CITY OF ALHAMBRA, CALIFORNIA, AMENDING CHAPTER 3.36 OF

  MUNICIPAL CODE, RELATED TO BIDDING AND CONTRACTS FOR
  PUBLIC PROJECTS, AND IMPLEMENTING THE CALIFORNIA UNIFORM
  CONSTRUCTION COST ACCOUNTING PROCEDURES FOR PUBLIC
  CONSTRUCTION PROJECTS
